extraction.name: XTREME-S
extraction.description: XTREME-S (Cross-lingual Transfer Evaluation of Multilingual Encoders for Speech) is an evaluation benchmark designed to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations across 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 speech domains, and 4 task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation, and retrieval.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: XTREME-S combines existing multilingual speech datasets (Multilingual LibriSpeech, VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, MINDS-14) with a new dataset, FLEURS. FLEURS collects speech recordings for 2009 n-way parallel sentences from the publicly available FLoRes dev and devtest sets across 102 languages, gathering between one and three recordings per sentence.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: FLEURS is complete at more than 97%, with potential missing recordings or replaced low-quality recordings to be addressed in subsequent versions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw text sentences from the FLoRes machine translation benchmark; read audiobooks from LibriVox (Multilingual LibriSpeech); European Parliament session recordings (VoxPopuli); spoken queries from the e-banking domain (MINDS-14); CoVoST-2; and candidate text pools from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For FLEURS, recordings were divided into train, dev, and test splits with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences respectively, ensuring speakers in the train sets differ from dev/test. For MINDS-14, monolingual sets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split. For speech retrieval, transcription candidate pools were augmented with 100k sentences per language from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: VoxPopuli was filtered to the 14 languages with more than 10 hours of data from the ASR task. Scripts are provided to download and reproduce preprocessing steps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Speech recordings were gathered based on prompt sentences from the FLoRes benchmark. Annotations for intent classification originate from MINDS-14 e-banking intent labels.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Between one and three recordings per sentence (2.3 on average) for FLEURS.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Updates, missing recording additions, or replacements of low-quality recordings for FLEURS will be made on Hugging Face. Additional test sets may be added in the future, and a submission leaderboard is maintained via dataset cards.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to make speech technology available across diverse languages to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet and facilitate sharing their content and culture outside their language cluster.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Performance discrepancies exist across geographical and language groups; models show substantially stronger results on Western European languages compared to Sub-Saharan African and South Asian languages, partially driven by disparities in available pre-training data volumes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Nonlinguistic and paralinguistic aspects of speech relevant to tasks such as speech synthesis or voice conversion are not evaluated. Speech classification tasks are prone to overfitting due to the disparity between rich acoustic input signals and small label spaces.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating universal multilingual speech representations, automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech-to-text translation (ST), language identification (LangID), intent classification, and speech-text retrieval.
